title: Correlate logs without inventing event order
question: What temporal order is supported after applying a signed clock correction and explicit uncertainty intervals?
scenario: Three correlated events share stable identifiers. IdP raw time is 10:00:00 with ±2 seconds uncertainty. Database raw time is 10:04:20; its signed clock offset is +4:00, meaning clock minus reference, so corrected time is 10:00:20 with ±2 seconds uncertainty. Egress corrected time is 10:00:40 with ±2 seconds uncertainty.
focalRelation: Preserve each raw timestamp; define signed offset as clock minus reference; compute corrected time as raw minus offset; expand corrected values by measured uncertainty; nonoverlapping intervals support only IdP before database before egress, while intent, causality, completeness, and any event with unknown offset remain unresolved.

nodes.label: DB · raw 10:04:20
nodes.detail: Signed offset +4:00 means the database clock is four minutes ahead of reference; corrected = raw − offset = 10:00:20.

nodes.label: Egress · corrected 10:00:40
nodes.detail: Corrected 10:00:40 ±2s gives [10:00:38, 10:00:42], with destination and correlation identifiers retained.

nodes.label: Signed correction rule
nodes.detail: Offset = clock − reference, so corrected time = raw − offset. Store raw time, signed offset, correction provenance, and uncertainty together.

nodes.label: Qualified temporal conclusion
nodes.detail: The measured intervals support IdP before DB before egress only; they do not prove intent, causality, or collection completeness.

edges.label: applies +4:00 as raw minus signed offset

states.title: Preserve raw observations
states.caption: Keep IdP raw 10:00:00, DB raw 10:04:20, and the egress observation with stable identifiers. Raw display order is not yet corrected event order.

states.title: Apply the signed correction
states.caption: Offset is clock minus reference. The DB clock is +4:00 ahead, so corrected DB time is 10:04:20 − 4:00 = 10:00:20.

states.title: Compare uncertainty intervals
states.caption: IdP [09:59:58,10:00:02], DB [10:00:18,10:00:22], and egress [10:00:38,10:00:42] are separated, so their measured temporal order is supported.

statuses.intervals: IdP interval < DB interval < egress interval

states.title: Bound the claim
states.caption: The intervals support IdP before DB before egress. They do not establish why the actions occurred, whether one caused another, or whether collection was complete.

variants.label: Unknown database offset

states.title: Offset evidence missing
states.caption: The DB raw time is preserved, but direction, magnitude, provenance, and uncertainty of its clock offset are unknown.

states.title: Keep only the supported partial order
states.caption: The IdP interval remains earlier than the egress interval. The DB event may overlap or fall outside either interval, so its exact precedence is unresolved.

statuses.intervals: IdP < egress supported · DB placement unresolved

states.title: Withdraw the unsupported claim
states.caption: Do not assert IdP<DB<egress. Preserve the raw DB record, obtain offset evidence if possible, and state only IdP before egress.

prediction.prompt: After applying the signed correction and ±2-second bounds, what may the investigation claim?

options.label: The IdP event caused the database action, which caused egress
options.feedback: Separated time intervals support temporal order only. They do not prove intent, causality, or completeness.

options.label: IdP [09:59:58,10:00:02] precedes DB [10:00:18,10:00:22], which precedes egress [10:00:38,10:00:42]
options.feedback: Correct. The nonoverlapping corrected intervals support that temporal order while leaving intent, causality, and completeness unresolved.

options.label: Use raw display order because uncertainty is only two seconds
options.feedback: The DB raw clock is four minutes ahead. Apply the signed correction before comparing uncertainty intervals.

prediction.hint: Preserve the raw observations, then check the signed-offset definition, provenance, and uncertainty before comparing time.

transfer.prompt: The DB raw event remains 10:04:20, but the signed offset and uncertainty cannot be established. What temporal statement survives?

options.label: Reuse the prior +4:00 correction and assert IdP before DB before egress
options.feedback: The prior correction is not evidence for this source state. Unknown direction and uncertainty remove exact DB placement.

options.label: Keep IdP before egress, preserve the DB raw time, and withdraw DB precedence until offset evidence exists
options.feedback: Correct. The known IdP and egress intervals remain ordered, while the DB event is unresolved and may overlap either interval.

options.label: Discard every source because one offset is unknown
options.feedback: Unknown DB timing limits cross-source sequence; it does not erase the IdP, egress, identity, action, or integrity evidence.

transfer.hint: Preserve the raw observation and identify which correction evidence is now unavailable before stating any order.

retry.prompt: Authentication and database logs have intact hashes, but their clocks differ by eleven minutes. Can the investigation assert event order?

options.label: Use hash-chain order to claim the authentication event preceded the database action
options.feedback: A hash chain orders records within its chain, not events across unsynchronized sources.

options.label: Discard both sources because clock drift makes every field unreliable
options.feedback: Clock drift limits temporal correlation but does not erase all source, action, or integrity evidence.

options.label: Preserve both sources, measure the clock offset, and qualify event-order claims
options.feedback: Correct. Hash integrity does not supply synchronized time or prove cross-source sequence.

retry.hint: Integrity protects records from change; temporal correlation depends on another control.

takeaway: Preserve raw time, apply signed corrections as corrected = raw − (clock − reference), retain uncertainty intervals, and claim only the temporal order those intervals support.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implements the reviewed native offset timeline with raw and corrected timestamps side by side: IdP 10:00:00±2s [09:59:58,10:00:02]; DB raw 10:04:20 with signed +4:00 correction to 10:00:20±2s [10:00:18,10:00:22]; egress 10:00:40±2s [10:00:38,10:00:42]. The measured branch supports only IdP<DB<egress temporal order. The unknown-offset branch withdraws DB precedence while retaining IdP<egress, and both branches reject intent, causality, or completeness claims.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Clock correction and uncertainty intervals can support temporal order when corrected ranges do not overlap. That order does not by itself prove causality, intent, or complete collection.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: Aligned corrected timestamps and uncertainty intervals let the learner compare ranges directly and see why order is supported while causality remains unproven.
